Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Bounded event audio

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Use Audio_Pool to play presentation cues with bounded voices and to match replayed events by identity. It owns a fixed set of positional and screen-space Godot players. audio_pool_init accepts their parent and capacities (12 world / 3 screen by default). The parent must outlive the pool. audio_pool_destroy stops playback, releases player-held streams and queues the child players for deletion.

An Audio_Cue supplies a borrowed stream, position, gain, pitch and spatial flag. Godot retains the stream while assigned to a player; the application keeps and releases its own loaded-resource references. audio_play handles immediate UI or forward-only presentation cues. A full pool steals a voice in round-robin order; work remains bounded and the pool counts steals.

For journal events, use audio_change(pool, consumption_log, change, cue, slot):

  • Begin consumes its event ID/effect slot once and starts playback.
  • Update adjusts the position of an active spatial voice without restarting it.
  • Confirm does not start another clip.
  • Cancel stops only a voice still tagged with that event ID/slot. A delayed cancel cannot stop a replacement voice after the pool has reused the player.

A consumed ID remains consumed after cancellation, completion or voice stealing. The library cannot undo samples already heard. The view.One_Shots ledger retains these consumed IDs in bounded tick buckets, independently of the active players. A reappearing Begin after correction is suppressed while retained. Once retired, old IDs remain expired rather than becoming new again.

Initialize the ledger with the presentation epoch/baseline and enough retained history/events per tick for the journal being consumed. one_shots_retire takes an explicitly safe monotonic frontier; it never silently evicts a live bucket to accept a colliding tick. Capacity is observable. one_shots_reset requires a newer epoch. Applications clear active voices and establish an appropriate new baseline when a session or playback epoch changes.

The pool rejects invalid cues before consuming a Begin. Volume is local to this pool and updates active voices; it does not modify the application's global master bus. Streams, players and consumption ledgers belong to presentation, never to a simulation frame or checkpoint.

tests/replay_audio/run.sh exercises actual Godot players, correction/confirmation, cancel/reappearance, voice reuse, resource release and nonzero mixer PCM captured through an AudioEffectCapture. Pure journal/ledger tests cover retention, capacity, retirement and epoch boundaries. WASM checks cover the same adapter.

Godot retires audio playback references asynchronously. Stop/detach the players and allow the engine loop to process retirement before a test expects zero resources at process exit. Hardware backend acceptance is separate from a headless Dummy mixer test. The included Godot-only capture probe also reproduced a silent/stalled CoreAudio mixer in this environment; no hardware-playback success is claimed.
